account: Today I read my appointment documents and attended morning office hours. The secretary said no new correspondence or business had arrived. I then came to the mill for the scheduled ten o'clock grain inspection, although no one has yet shown me the grain stores or given me a report about them. The unusual news is several townsfolk repeating an unclear report of a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. Townsfolk 21 said the baker and innkeeper were there, and one version also included freight. I do not yet know what changed, when it happened, or why; it might concern transport or deliveries, but that is only a possibility, not something I have confirmed. My neighbour says the bridge was clear when they crossed this morning, which does not establish whether any arrangements have changed. I should seek a direct explanation from the baker, innkeeper, or freight rather than treat the repeated reports as proof. Today's other confirmed business includes tea at the neighbour's dockside cottage at fifteen hundred, and meeting the innkeeper at my office at seventeen forty-five before going to the great hall at eighteen to discuss the inn's service to town. I have no evidence that this scheduled meeting is connected to the bakery reports.
